attempts.summary: Joined node2's and node3's separate segments off node1 into a single L2 domain: created a Linux bridge (br0) on node1 spanning eth1 (toward node2) and eth2 (toward node3), assigned node2/node3 static IPs 192.168.50.11/.12 on their enp8s0 NICs (via nmcli, since NetworkManager was reconciling away manual `ip addr` assignments), and verified node1 forwards frames transparently at L2 rather than routing. Persisted the bridge config in /etc/network/interfaces.d/br0 on node1. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all three nodes: each was restarted individually, boot identity change was proven via /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, and post-restart recovery (bridge auto-recreation on node1; static IP persistence and L2 connectivity on node2/node3) was directly verified.
